title: Ulysses and the Sirens
subtitle: Listen without dying
subject: mythologie
description: The Sirens promise absolute knowledge. Odysseus is the only mortal to hear their song and survive, thanks to a ruse that has become a model of self-control.

hero.hook: Their song promises to know everything. Everyone who listens to it dies. Ulysses wants to hear… and stay alive.

blocks.text: In the twelfth canto of the **Odyssey**, Ulysses must pass near the . Their voice is so beautiful that it overrides the will. Sailors who approach run aground and die. **[[Mermaids]]**

It's not just an adventure at sea. It's the duel between the thirst for knowledge and the danger of giving in. Thanks to his , his cunning intelligence, Ulysses becomes the only mortal to taste this forbidden pleasure without losing his life. [[Metis]]
In **Homer**, the Mermaids are not fish women. They are half-woman, half-bird creatures. Their island is littered with sailors' bones. The beauty of the song contrasts with the horror of the shore.

blocks.caption: The island of the Sirens: irresistible melody, deadly shore.

blocks.text: In Greek cities, Sirens were often carved on tombs. They were seen as muses from the afterlife, accompanying the souls of the dead.

Their trap is not only sensual. They promise **absolute knowledge**: everything that happened in , everything that happens on earth. For Ulysses, curious above all, it is the supreme temptation, more dangerous than a monster to defeat. [[Trojan War]]

sections.title: The wax, the mast and the plan

blocks.text: The magician **Circé** warned him. Ulysses prepares a precise strategy. He plugs his companions' ears with **beeswax**. They shouldn't hear anything. He wants to listen.

blocks.caption: Ulysses tied to the mast, the only one to hear the song of the Sirens.

blocks.text: It gets **attached to the mast**. Clear order: if he asks to be released, on the contrary we must tighten the bonds. When the song rises, Ulysses loses his calm and shouts to be untied. His men, deaf and faithful to the plan, only obey the rational Odysseus from before, not the captivated Odysseus of the moment. The ship passes.

sections.title: Attach yourself in advance so as not to give in

blocks.text: This scene illustrates what the social sciences call the . We know that we will be weak in the face of temptation. So we limit our options ourselves before getting there. [[Precommitment]]
In 1990, NASA and ESA named a probe **Ulysses**. Like the hero, she leaves the known roads to explore the poles of the Sun.

Nobel Prize-winning economist **Richard Thaler** draws on this image. Humans are not always rational. He needs a , a “helping hand”, or rules that protect him from himself: automatic transfer to savings, applications that block networks. Like Ulysses, we attach ourselves to the mast in the face of modern sirens. [[Nudge]]
In **Middle Ages**, the image changes. The bird woman becomes a fish woman. The Church reads Sirens as symbols of lust. Ulysses' mast is sometimes compared to the cross: a shield against temptation.

In Homer, however, the issue was not carnal desire, but knowledge. Odysseus is neither a saint nor a simple adventurer. He is a man who uses intelligence to navigate between the desire for absolutes and the need to survive.
